summary: The school district urges the FCC to preserve and strengthen the E-Rate program, rejecting proposals to sunset or eliminate it, and instead proposes preserving and modernizing the program to meet the needs of schools and students. The text expresses opposition to limiting or sunsetting E-Rate, emphasizing its importance for providing connectivity to schools and libraries. It urges the Commission to protect E-Rate to ensure students have access to necessary tools for learning.

claims.argument: Federal Communications Commission should reject any proposal to sunset or eliminate the E-Rate program
claims.evidence_quote: Reject any proposal to sunset or eliminate the E-Rate program; Reject proposals that would unnecessarily narrow E-Rate eligibility or restrict support based solely on geography or other criteria that would leave students without adequate support; Preserve support for the connectivity and internal network infrastructure schools need to provide reliable educational access; and Work with schools and other stakeholders to strengthen and modernize E-Rate rather than reduce its role in public education.

claims.argument: Limiting or sunsetting E-Rate would reduce funding for broadband infrastructure and connectivity in schools and libraries.
claims.evidence_quote: al access; and Work with schools and other stakeholders to strengthen and modernize E-Rate rather than reduce its role in public education. E-Rate has enabled schools (public and private) and libraries to build and maintain the connectivity necessary for students and patrons to participate fully in modern education. As our nation seeks to prepare students for college, careers, and an increasingly technology-driven economy, now is not the time to undermine the very program and related infrastructure that makes those opportunities possible.
